section_summary.extract_value: This General discussion summarizes the development and psychometric evaluation of the Caregiver Eating Messages Scale (CEMS), which assesses perceived restrictive/critical and pressure-to-eat caregiver messages. It states that multidisciplinary experts reviewed the items and that a psychometric investigation supported a two-factor structure with internal consistency and stability over a 4-week period. The section does not mention 'Study 1', 'Experiment 2', or multiple sample subsets.
section_summary.evidence_source: "This study incrementally contributes to the literature on caregiver eating messages, body image, and eating behavior by presenting the CEMS, which measures individuals' perceptions of their caregivers' tendency to restrict food intake/make critical comments about their eating and impose pressure on them to eat certain foods." "A psychometric investigation of the CEMS indicated that it conformed to its hypothesized two-factor structure, measuring restrictive/critical caregiver eating messages and pressure to eat messages, and yielded internally consistent and stable scores over a 4-week period."

section_summary.extract_value: This section describes the development and validation of the Caregiver Eating Messages Scale (CEMS), which assesses perceptions of caregivers' restrictive/critical and pressure-to-eat messages. Experts reviewed items, and a psychometric investigation found a two-factor structure with internally consistent and stable scores over a 4-week period.
section_summary.evidence_source: Text: "This study incrementally contributes to the literature on caregiver eating messages, body image, and eating behavior by presenting the CEMS, which measures individuals' perceptions of their caregivers' tendency to restrict food intake/make critical comments about their eating and impose pressure on them to eat certain foods. Experts of various disciplines... evaluated the items... A psychometric investigation of the CEMS indicated that it conformed to its hypothesized two-factor structure... and yielded internally consistent and stable scores over a 4-week period."

Asset Caption.extract_value: Fig. 3. Test of the negative body attitudes and maladaptive eating model. Total scale and subscale scores serve as observed variables in the model. RCM = Restrictive Critical Messages subscale of the Caregiver Eating Messages Scale, PSPS-Family = Family subscale of the Perceived Sociocultural Pressures Scale, EDI-BD = Body Dissatisfaction subscale of the Eating Disorder Inventory-2, and EAT-26 = Eating Attitudes Test-26. Path coefficients above the path are for women; path coefficients below the path are for men. *p < .05.
